findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are hard-coded in plaintext in the EC2 user_data script, which is stored in Terraform state and retrievable via the instance metadata service or describe-instance API calls, leading to credential compromise.
The security group allows inbound SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing administrative access to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or exploitation attempts against the host.

The security group allows inbound HTTP (port 80) from 0.0.0.0/0 with unrestricted egress to 0.0.0.0/0 as well; combined with the subnet's public IP assignment, this maximizes the internet-facing attack surface for the web tier with no segmentation.

The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, so data stored on the volume is not encrypted at rest, risking exposure of sensitive data if the underlying storage is compromised or improperly decommissioned.
The EBS snapshot inherits the unencrypted state of its source volume, so snapshot data remains unencrypted at rest and could be shared or restored without protection.

map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IPs to instances launched in this subnet (including web_host), increasing the attack surface by making them directly internet-reachable.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IPs to instances launched in this subnet, increasing the attack surface by making them directly internet-reachable.

The S3 bucket storing VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration (no aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration), leaving potentially sensitive network traffic metadata unencrypted at rest.
The S3 bucket has no bucket policy, ACL restriction, or public access block configuration defined, leaving it potentially exposed to public access depending on account-level defaults.
